name: multipart-form-parsing-p4
prompt: how do I correctly parse a multipart form upload without buffering the whole request body in memory

chunks.content: decided to parse the multipart body incrementally off the socket, writing each file part straight to a temp file on disk so a large upload never inflates the heap
the parser reads the boundary delimiter from the Content-Type header and splits parts on it, treating the trailing CRLF before each boundary as part of the framing not the payload
the login form posts username and password as url-encoded fields and we validate them server-side before issuing a token
the submit button now shows a progress bar while the request is in flight
we cap each individual part at 25 MB and reject the whole request early once the cumulative size crosses 100 MB, before reading further bytes, to bound resource use
added an index on uploads(user_id, created_at) for the file history view
the checkout form validates the postal code field against a regex and shows an inline error if the multipart of the address is malformed
background workers pull jobs from the queue in batches of 50
we sanitize the filename from each part's Content-Disposition, stripping path separators so an upload cannot escape the destination directory
non-file parts like a description text field are decoded with the charset from the part header and surfaced as ordinary form fields to the handler
added p99 latency tracking to the checkout endpoint
the weekly digest email is assembled from the activity feed each Monday
narrowed the read-only token scope so it can no longer mutate resources
warm the homepage cache on deploy to avoid a cold first hit
